writeup: TIC 96687087 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 7.73 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse causes a 10.76% dimming of the star's light, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal ranks highly in automated significance metrics, with a BLS detection signal-to-noise of 610.7 and pixel-level confirmation showing a peak signal-to-noise of 67.6. However, an important open question remains: the odd and even eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the BLS algorithm initially measured half the true orbital period. The centroid offset of 0.6 arcseconds from the target position was measured but does not affect the timing analysis. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a potentially novel object for further study.
